items.title: AAP, Authors Guild Applaud Decision in ROSS Copyright Infringement Case
items.excerpt: An appeals judge backed a Delaware court ruling that found the now-defunct AI startup Ross Intelligence's unauthorized copying of text from Thomson Reuters's Westlaw was not fair use; AAP and the Authors Guild hailed it as a precedent for AI training cases.

history_match.title: Authors Guild, Co-Plaintiffs Seek Summary Judgment in OpenAI Case

items.title: We Banned the Soul from the Building: On AI, Spiritual Life, and Sustainable Practices for Writing
items.excerpt: The literary world is finally asking what a human writer can do that artificial intelligence cannot; this essay argues the answer lies beyond technique, in spiritual life and sustainable writing practice.

items.title: Can Better Wording Fix the “Made With AI” Problem? New 2026 Research Says It's Complicated
items.excerpt: New 2026 research on how 'Made with AI' labels affect reader trust finds that rewording disclosures does not simply fix the penalty audiences apply to AI-assisted content.

items.title: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
items.excerpt: OpenAI is launching 'textGrain' watermarking of ChatGPT-generated text in the EU to comply with the AI Act, but says it won't be the global default yet; a provenance shift with direct implications for AI-written manuscripts and submissions.

items.title: The Representation Is Not the Scholarship
items.excerpt: The problem with AI in scholarly publishing may not be that machines are growing more intelligent, but that we are amplifying a capable yet limited form of cognition and mistaking the written representation for the scholarship itself.

items.title: Ask the Chefs: What Would You Have Done Differently About Open Access/Open Science if You Predicted the World as it Exists Today? Part 1
items.excerpt: Scholarly Kitchen chefs reconsider open-access strategy in hindsight, with AI training on openly licensed research a central theme of what they would do differently.

history_match.title: Ask the Chefs: AI and Copyright Licensing

items.title: Around the Book World: Monday, October 5th, 2026
items.excerpt: Roundup highlights: a Proyecto451 review of 40+ publishers' AI policies finds two strategies (license catalogs to AI firms vs. build in-house tools); ElevenLabs' aggregator-led audiobook strategy via De Marque, Bookwire and StreetLib; a Norwegian debut novel written entirely by hand to prove it is not AI.

items.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: The Asia Stage Returns
items.excerpt: Frankfurt's Asia Stage program will cover Asian markets, authors of interest to Western publishers, and how these countries' publishing industries are engaging with AI.

items.title: Elredo Voice's AI is making publisher backlists worth recording
items.excerpt: Elredo Voice was built to help publishers turn the thousands of books sitting in their backlists into audio using AI narration.
